# Graph Community Detection Algorithms for RAG

> Graph clustering mechanics including Leiden, Louvain, and Infomap for constructing hierarchical community summaries in retrieval pipelines.

## Core Findings

- The Leiden algorithm resolves Louvain's fundamental defect of producing disconnected or weakly connected communities by introducing an explicit sub-community refinement step that guarantees partition connectivity. [Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-019-41695-z]
- Hierarchical community detection partitions large knowledge graphs into multi-scale clusters (from fine-grained sub-communities C3 to macro-thematic clusters C0), establishing the structured partition hierarchy required for multi-level GraphRAG summarization. [Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130]
- Modularity optimization (Newman-Girvan modularity Q) exhibits a resolution limit where communities smaller than sqrt(2L) cannot be resolved, necessitating Constant Potts Model (CPM) or resolution parameter tuning in RAG pipelines. [Source: https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.0605965104]
